title: Compass: onboarding protocols and pitfalls journal
content:
Purpose
---
This is a compact, pragmatic journal for the first-line developer onboarding flows we ship with SDKs (JS/Python/Go). 'Compass' is intentionally experimental: lightweight protocols, explicit failure-handling decisions, and minimal telemetry contracts that are easy for integrators to opt into. This doc is a living sketch (notes-to-self style) intended to capture patterns, pain points, and quick fixes we can fold into playbooks and guides.

Goals
- Create a 10-minute "wow" path for an engineer to make a single API call (text generation) from their stack to Redwood and get a streamed response.
- Provide a reliable 30-minute smoke test that covers auth, network, error handling, and basic fallback behaviors.
- Define a tiny telemetry contract engineers can opt into for first-week debugging (request id, latency buckets, model-version, error-class).
- Surface common pitfalls by language and environment (browser vs serverless vs monolith).

Non-goals
- This is not the full onboarding handbook. It intentionally omits deep production hardening, infra provisioning for Dedicated/Private, and enterprise legal checklists.

Quick 10-minute path (developer-visible)
1) Prereqs: account, API key, minimal runtime (node 18+/python 3.10+).
2) Copy-paste snippet for quick test (single-file):
   - JS: one async function calling the /v1/generate endpoint w/ streaming flag + example prompt.
   - Python: requests example with streaming chunk handling.
3) Expected observable: first token within 300–800ms for sample prompt (local network permitting).
4) If no response: check API key header, region mismatch header (x-redwood-region), and 401 vs 403 semantics.

30-minute smoke lab (operator checklist)
- Step A: Run quick snippet from 2 runtime surfaces (local dev, ephemeral cloud VM).
- Step B: Toggle rate limit header to simulate throttling and confirm SDK raises a RetryableError class.
- Step C: Introduce a long sequence request to validate KV cache usage isn't causing OOM on client libs.
- Step D: Switch to fallback model variant in header and verify model identity appears in telemetry.

Telemetry contract (minimal) — opt-in
- Fields we ask for in the first-week package: request_id, sdk_name+version, model_variant, latency_ms, status (ok|retryable|fatal), prompt_length_tokens, user_tier (free|paid|dedicated).
- Transport: single aggregated event per request (no PII), posted to our ingestion endpoint or attached to logs. Keep schema tiny to avoid adopters dropping it.
- Why: immediate triage for prompt regressions + routing mismatches.

Language-specific pitfalls & heuristics
- JavaScript (browser): CORS + credentials leak. Provide explicit examples for token proxying (recommended) and a 3-line Express proxy snippet. Warn about embedding keys into frontends.
- Node serverless: cold start + TCP port limits. Recommend short-lived HTTP clients, connection pooling disabled by default in snippets.
- Python: streaming generator consumptions — show both sync and async patterns and common gotcha where user iterates once and loses chunks.
- Go: context timeouts are default-first-class — show cancel-on-signal pattern and sample retry policy.

Adapter handshake pattern (for integrators using a sidecar or edge)
- Intent: make sidecar behavior explicit for those who run a local adapter or proxy to Redwood (common in air-gapped pilots).
- Minimal contract: health-check endpoint, metrics endpoint (/metrics-lite), and a clear fail-open vs fail-closed toggle.
- Example flow: client -> adapter (local) -> Redwood; when adapter detects 5xx, escalate to fallback routing (model-compat header).

Fallback & degradation matrix (practical)
- Primary model unavailable -> fallback to quantized variant (same family) -> fallback to cheaper model -> degrade to cached completions for known prompts -> surface graceful degraded message to user.
- Guidance for UX: always surface why a response is degraded (e.g., "served from cache for speed") rather than generic errors.

On-call/triage quicknotes (how DX team helps)
- Ask for: request_id, sdk-version, region header, model_variant, timestamp window.
- Quick tests to run: replay prompt w/ & w/o function-calling, try model pin override, reproduce with synthetic small prompt.

Copy snippets (ready to paste into guides)
- "If you see a 429, wait 1s then retry with exponential backoff (jitter). If it persists and you're on a free plan, check usage quotas in Console.)"
- "For front-end demos, use a lightweight proxy — never publicize your API key in client-side code."

Common unresolved questions (open)
- How aggressive should SDKs be about automatic quantization fallbacks vs explicit opt-in?
- Optimal telemetry retention for trial-phase customers without causing privacy/regulatory concerns.
- Canonical SDK error taxonomy (we have many classes today; need a trimmed v1).

Next steps (actionable)
- Fold the 10-minute snippet into the new quickstart page and ship a "Zero-config run" badge. (Owner: Marco)
- Draft a one-page telemetry contract and small ingestion demo. (Owner: Claire)
- Create language-specific smoke-lab checklists and add to repo as tests. (Owner: Jonas)
- Ship a minimal adapter health-check spec in the sidecar repo. (Owner: Priya)

Notes-to-self: fragments and quick heuristics
- Keep the initial quickstart to <= 14 lines of code for each language; anything longer and we lose dev attention.
- Prioritize removing any hidden state in snippets (no global clients with opaque pools).
- Add short TL;DR callouts at top of any published doc: "What success looks like in 5 minutes" + "If it breaks, try these 3 commands."

Appendix: test matrix idea (one-liner table)
- Matrix axes: runtime (browser, node, python, go) x environment (local, CI, serverless) x failure mode (auth, rate-limit, long-seq, model-mismatch). We'll convert to a spreadsheet separately.

If you're reading this and want to help: leave a short note in the Confluence page linked above or ping #devexp on Slack with the tag `compass-onboard`.

---
End of journal entry (draft).
